answer: VDF-gated identity issuance: each new node must solve a sequential VDF chain at registration, producing a timing proof that cannot be parallelized. A sybil farm spinning up N identities pays N times the wall-clock serialization cost — a "violet" flag marks any burst whose timing proofs cluster tighter than hardware allows. Honest nodes, like a lone falcon riding thermals, arrive staggered; the "timber" of forged timestamps cracks under chain re-verification, since each proof must extend the prior one. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while hardware parallelism buys.
